author: Eurogamer
text:
Xbox Cloud Gaming's new hourly cap is reportedly set exactly where Microsoft stops making money on it

A new report suggests that Xbox has capped its cloud gaming usage to 15 hours for Game Pass Ultimate subscribers because that's when the service stops being profitable.

author: Eurogamer
text:
Sony clarifies PlayStation disc production is dropping by 10 percent in 2028, not to 10 percent

Sony has pushed back on a wave of reports suggesting PlayStation disc manufacturing is about to be gutted by 90 percent after comments from a Sony DADC executive were allegedly misunderstood.

Read more

author: Eurogamer
text:
Gamescom apologises for how it initially responded to indie developer hardware thefts

Gamescom has apologised for the way it "communicated about the theft of hardware belonging to several indie developers" last week, admitting, "our first response did not strike the right tone, and it did not show the people affected the empathy they deserved".

author: Eurogamer
text:
White House launches Arcade.gov, a minigame site parodying immigration enforcement and border security

The White House has launched Arcade.Gov, a website of browser minigames built around Donald Trump's immigration and border policies.

Read more

author: Eurogamer
text:
BioWare doesn't need advice for Mass Effect 4, says veteran designer, as long as "people get out of the way"

Original Mass Effect cinematic designer and Mass Effect 2 lead cinematic designer Armando Troisi has insisted the current BioWare team doesn't need outside advice on developing the next installment because so many of the people who built the original trilogy are still at the studio.

author: Eurogamer
text:
Gen-AI controversy aside, Crazy Taxi: World Tour feels like classic arcade Sega - and it's an absolute blast

Crazy Taxi was not my favourite Dreamcast game (please don't ask me to choose between the triumphant rhythm triptych of Rez, Space Channel 5, and Samba de Amigo, however), but there's a specific bit of it that's forever seared into my brain: the giddy thrill of cresting over that one San-Francisco-inspired hill and barreling down toward the ocean, all while The Offspring's All I Want 'Yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah, yeah'ed me into a state of gaming nirvana.

text:
What we've been playing - "Well this is embarrassing, we're wearing the same outfit!"

Unluckily for you all, Bertie's having a well-earned long weekend (possibly skiing, possibly jumping on the spot, possibly just having a nice lie down after the chaos of it all), meaning you're stuck with me on intro duties for What We've Been Playing this time around.

author: Eurogamer
text:
After AI slop accusations, Humankind 2 studio says its new trailer was definitely "made by humankind" and at least five chickens

A large portion of the internet pointed their virtual fingers at Humankind 2's new trailer and shouted 'AI slop!' Developer Amplitude Studios is now denying those claims and has even released a behind-the-scenes clip to prove a whole human crew (plus five chickens) made the Gamescom ONL reveal.

Read more

author: Eurogamer
text:
It looks like No Man's Sky's next update is imminent as Sean Murray breaks out the emojis again - and fans reckon it's a big one

Yes, it's time to brace yourself once more, No Man's Sky fans: Sean Murray is delving into his big bag of emojis, indicating - with reliable certainty - the exploratory space sim's highly anticipated 10th anniversary update will be with us very soon. And there's hope among the playerbase that Cosmos, as the update was previously confirmed to be called, might be a big 'un.

author: Eurogamer
text:
Nearly a decade on, legendary director Hideki Kamiya says he's "100% serious" about reviving Xbox's canned Scalebound

Hideki Kamiya was being super serious about resurrecting Scalebound, PlatinumGames' dragon-filled romp that was cancelled by Xbox nearly a decade ago.
